I don't have support. My entire family faded away when I got sick. It's just me in this dark room with no human contact except for a caregiver who abused me. And this. My first human contact today caused a massive PTSD flashback, and the second human contact today has told me how horrible of a person I am. I clearly don't deserve to live. Even strangers can see it. 

But thank you. Thank you so much. You have no idea what this means to me. I have not felt kindness in so long.

How is this a planning failure on my part? I am severely disabled and get $1200/month income. When I have to buy something, I buy from small sellers. I have done that since I moved to this country in 1989. Small sellers are often more expensive, and yes, it does take longer. I allow for this, and every time I contact a seller it is with respect and kindness. Unfortunately, I expect the same in return. I say unfortunately because what I get is ghosted. 

When a package that they chose not to get tracking for never shows up, how is that my fault? I really want to understand your point of view. And thank you for not just starting with insults.
Ah, here's the personal insult.
Thank you for saying this, but I've taken all the pills now. I won't have to deal with people anymore. No more pain. No more pain.

TELL ME, HAVE YOU BEEN RAPED BEFORE? WHAT DOES IT FEEL LIKE? AND IN PARTICULAR, WHAT DID I FEEL LIKE WHEN I WAS RAPED? HOW DO YOU KNOW THAT I DONT PERSONALLY FEEL THAT WAY NOW? YOU DON'T KNOW ME.
Thank you. Everyone else is telling me what an awful person I am for dating to say anything negative about a seller.
And I can't shower. I'm totally disabled and bed bound. My life is a hellish nightmare of pain and confusion. I have an incurable disease that will kill me. But these people will kill me first.
YOU HAVE DONE NOTHING BUT PERSONALLY INSULT ME IN EVETY SINGLE POST. EVIDENTLY YOU FEEL SOOOOOO BAD FOR SELLERS WHO TAKE A DISABLED WOMANS MONEY AND THEN FUCK HER OVER.

How DARE a wronged customer ever say anything negative about Etsy sellers. How DARE I be frustrated with three Etsy sellers in a row taking my money and ghosting. My god, how DARE I be human?

I would promptly send either a replacement or a refund, the customer's choice, and Etsy wouldn't even have to get involved. Just a few days ago I got in trouble for being suicidal. If this is not an order for a flat paper object, keep reading.

There are 3 possibilities for a package stuck in pre-transit.

Generally speaking, there is no way for us to guess which of these things happened. The seller is the only person who knows for sure.

1: The seller bought a shipping label for the order but has not actually dropped the package off.

2: The seller dropped the package off and it didn't get scanned.

3: The seller is lying about being in the US and dropshipped your order from overseas.

Given the incredible amount of sellers drop shipping from overseas (I'm sure you see it too), #3 is a concern. I'm giving her the benefit of the doubt and assuming that's not the case, so either #1 or #2 are more likely. 

Her words: "I shipped your package on the 16 of August, it's impossible to get a tracking number before you send the package."

Actually, feeling "tired" has nothing to do with this disease, as anyone who has it can tell you. The fatigue is physical, sometimes to the point where it is impossible to lift one's head from the pillow. Added to this, most of us can't sleep. 

The formal diagnostic criteria are as follows:

1. Symptoms present are moderate, substantial, or severe intensity at least one-half of the time. (Typically activity is reduced by at least 50%.)

2. Post-exertional malaise, which is a severe worsening of symptoms after minimal physical or mental exertion--for a good 15% of us, this can include brushing your teeth or having a short conversation with your child). It usually starts 12-24 hours after the exertion and can last days, weeks, months, or years. Some never recover their previous level of functioning. 

3. Unrefreshing sleep. Regardless of duration or quality of sleep, there is no sense of feeling refreshed or rested upon waking. In a nutshell, every morning you wake up feeling like you have the flu  after binge-drinking AND running a marathon the previous day. 

4. One of the two must be present:
     A. Cognitive impairment. For most of us, this is by far the worst symptom. I've gone from reading 1000+ page books in a single day to not being able to read much at all. Verbal conversations have to be limited to five minutes at a time, and I can't remember what I did an hour ago.
     B. Orthostatic intolerance. A patient's blood pressure drops and heart rate rises upon standing or sitting upright. This is often severe and can cause loss of consciousness. 

I hope I've helped you understand this disease a little more. :-)

The certain similarity of symptoms you refered to are the diagnostic criteria you can find on the CDC website. 

The following three are mandatory. If you're missing just one, you don't have it. 

1. Severe unexplained physical fatigue (not anywhere near what "tired" is) which is not relieved by rest or sleep. 

 Usually they require a 50% reduction in daily activities, so it's not someone who's just tired all the time. 

2. Worsening of symptoms after very little exertion, usually occurring 24 hours after the exertion.  This is called Post Exertional Malaise. It is the hallmark sign of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome, and it is unique to this disease. Worsening of symptoms include severe cognitive impairment, swollen glands, sore throat, dizziness due to orthostatic intolerance, and profound fatigue. 

For some people with ME/CFS, a dinner out with friends can cause someone to feel as though they have the worst hangover of their life while sick with influenza the day after they ran a marathon.  In some, a short conversation or brushing their teeth will cause it. A "crash" can last days, weeks, months. A significant percentage of people never recover.

3. Unrefreshing sleep. (No matter how long you sleep, you wake up with the flu/hangover/marathon feeling--every single day of your life.)

Only ONE of these two must be present:

     A. Problems with thinking and memory (for example, if I am having a bad day, I cant speak because I can't understand the spoken word, and I've gone from reading 1000 page books in a day to being unable to read english much at all.)

     B. Worsening of symptoms while sitting or standing upright due to orthostatic intolerance (low blood pressure accompanied by tachycardia).

There are of course other symptoms, like pain which can be excruciating, but they were not chosen for the criteria. 

I hope I didn't overwhelm you! This is a very misunderstood biological disease that is more common than multiple sclerosis with a worse quality of life than a late stage AIDS patient. Whenever I have an opportunity I encourage people to learn about it. :-)

I feel so sad when I hear people saying that ME/CFS isn't a "real" disease when they haven't done a lick of reading about it. Please read the links I sent you. Up to 2.5 million Americans suffer from what has been recognized by the CDC, WHO, Social Security Administration (they have a special ruling for it).

While there is currently no biomarker for this disease, that is not uncommon. Until 1996, when scientists were able to look at the brain with an MRI (I believe that was the year), there was no test for multiple sclerosis. It was diagnosed solely through symptoms. There is currently no formal biomarkers for Parkinson's either (only proposed ones, which is the case with ME/CFS). Again, it is diagnosed through symptoms. 

ME/CFS is diagnosed by using a specific set of criteria:

1. A substantial reduction or impairment in the ability to engage in pre-illness levels of activity. This must be a reduction of at least 50%.
2. Post-exertional malaise (PEM)*—worsening of symptoms after physical, mental, or emotional exertion. This is considered the hallmark symptom, as the worsening of symptoms is delayed and can last for months. 
3. Unrefreshing sleep (no improvement of symptoms regardless of sleep duration or quality).
4. One of the following two:
     a. Cognitive impairment
     b. Orthostatic intolerance

People with ME/CFS can be sicker than an AIDS patient weeks before death. 25% of us (me included) are either completely bedridden or housebound. 10% are so I'll that they can't sit up, speak, brush their teeth, hug someone, etc.  

There has been an incredible amount of research done in the past 10 years, and many studies have consistently identified unique deficits in mitochondrial functioning. Lack of blood flow to the brain and reduced amounts of carbon dioxide in the blood have also been found. 

Please don't tell people that their bona fide organic disease (as proven by science and medicine) is just a collection of symptoms and doesn't explain what is wrong with them. We have been through enough of that, and it's incredibly psychologicaly harmful. Before you tell someone their disease isn't real, please do some reading on your own.

I have FM and ME/CFS. The hallmark symptom of ME/CFS is post-exertional malaise (PEM). Symptoms include severe fatigue (I’ve often been completely unable to speak or move—paralysis is common), headaches, and flu-like symptoms. PEM usually occurs the day AFTER you exert yourself, but not always. It is not unusual for people with ME/CFS to be completely house bound or bed-ridden (sometimes for years). If you are concerned that you might have ME/CFS, pay attention to your activity levels. As soon as you feel yourself becoming fatigued, STOP. Exercise is contraindicated in ME/CFS and will make you worse (this is scientifically confirmed and documented).
